source: AI Feynman (Udrescu, Tegmark 2020) AI Feynman: a physics-inspired method for symbolic regression
finding: Recursive symbolic regression that fits a neural net, then tests for symmetry, separability and compositionality to split the problem into smaller ones.
numbers: Finds all 100 Feynman Lectures equations; the best earlier public software (Eureqa) solved 71. On 20 harder 'bonus' equations, success rose from 15% to 90%.
limits: Kepler needed about 4 years and 40 failed ovoid fits to find the ellipse (paper intro). Test set is textbook physics, likely in LLM training data (see LLM-SRBench). Needs low-dimensional clean data; noise hurts.
agent_relevance: Discovery is search made tractable by exploiting structure. Our schema can split a hard question into separable parts before searching.

source: Udrescu et al. (2020) AI Feynman 2.0: Pareto-optimal symbolic regression exploiting graph modularity
finding: Adds generalised-symmetry discovery from network gradients, normalizing flows for distributions, and a Pareto frontier of accuracy vs complexity.
numbers: Abstract claims typically orders of magnitude more robust to noise and bad data than v1, and solves formulas that stumped v1.
limits: Compares against its own predecessor; no LLM involved. Recursive Pareto-pruning after each merge speeds the search.
agent_relevance: Keep a frontier of candidate hypotheses scored on fit vs simplicity, not one best guess.

source: Cranmer (2023) Interpretable machine learning for science with PySR and SymbolicRegression.jl
finding: Open-source multi-population evolutionary symbolic regression: evolve, simplify, optimize constants, with independent islands and simulated annealing; Julia backend for speed.
numbers: Software description, not one benchmark; it is the standard baseline in later LLM equation work.
limits: Genetic search needs very many evaluations (LLM-SR baselines ran 2M+ iterations). Pareto front of accuracy vs complexity used to pick an interpretable model.
agent_relevance: Cheap evaluators plus mutation work for equations. Our agent should use a code or data check as evaluator where one exists.

source: Shojaee et al. (2024) LLM-SR: Scientific equation discovery via programming with LLMs
finding: LLM proposes equation skeletons as Python programs using domain priors; parameters are fitted to data; an evolutionary buffer feeds the best programs back into the prompt.
numbers: Four new tasks (2 nonlinear oscillators, E. coli growth, stress-strain). LLM-SR beat PySR, uDSR, DSR, NeSymReS, E2E in NMSE with 2.5K iterations vs 2M+ for baselines. E. coli OOD NMSE about 0.0037 for the best variant while other methods had OOD NMSE above 1.
limits: Transformer SR models did poorly on the novel datasets. Gap to baselines larger out of domain. Backbones GPT-3.5 and Mixtral; some Mixtral E. coli OOD results were worse (5.46), so not uniform. Tasks are small and author-designed.
agent_relevance: Scientific priors in the LLM plus an external fitting check beat blind search. Supports propose-then-test with a real evaluator.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) LLM-SRBench: A new benchmark for scientific equation discovery with LLMs
finding: Benchmark of 239 problems: 111 LSR-Transform (Feynman equations rewritten into unfamiliar forms) and 128 LSR-Synth (synthetic mixes of known and novel terms) over 4 domains.
numbers: Best system reaches only 31.5% symbolic accuracy on LSR-Transform and 28.1% on LSR-Synth. A 100-problem Feynman control showed sharp error drops consistent with memorisation (Llama-3.1-8B sampling).
limits: Symbolic accuracy checked by GPT-4o with 94.6% agreement with humans on sampled problems. LLM judge for symbolic match; memorisation evidence is indirect.
agent_relevance: Old-benchmark success partly reflects recall. Discovery claims need unseen or transformed problems.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs generate novel research ideas? A large-scale human study with 100+ NLP researchers
finding: Blind expert review of 49 human-written ideas, 49 LLM-agent ideas, and 49 LLM ideas reranked by a human, across 7 NLP topics.
numbers: 79 reviewers, 298 reviews, 104 participants total. Mean novelty 4.84 human, 5.64 AI, 5.81 AI+human rerank (1-10). Ideas as unit: AI novelty p=0.03, rerank p=0.00. Excitement: AI 5.18 (p=0.08), rerank 5.45 (p=0.00). Feasibility and effectiveness not significantly different; overall rerank 5.32 p=0.06.
limits: Judged before execution; only NLP prompting topics; low reviewer agreement; human writers may not have offered their best ideas. Abstract: AI ideas judged more novel (p < 0.05) but slightly weaker on feasibility.
agent_relevance: LLMs can generate ideas that look novel. Novelty alone is not the goal; schema must also check feasibility.

source: Si et al. (2024) Idea generation study: diversity and self-evaluation failures
finding: Over-generation hits a diversity wall, and LLMs rank ideas poorly.
numbers: Of 4000 seed ideas per topic, only about 200 were non-duplicates at cosine similarity 0.8; accumulation plateaus. Claude-3.5-Sonnet predicted accept vs reject pairs at 71.4%, GPT-4o 61.1%, Claude-3-Opus 63.5%. Only 17 of 49 reranked ideas overlapped with the AI-ranked top.
limits: Agent: retrieval of up to 120 papers, 4000 seeds, dedup, pairwise ranking with N=5 rounds. Dedup threshold chosen by manual inspection; one topic set.
agent_relevance: Sampling more is not enough: diversity saturates. Need operators that force different frames, and external checks rather than self-ranking.

source: Si et al. (2025) The ideation-execution gap: execution outcomes of LLM vs human research ideas
finding: Follow-up: 43 experts each spent over 100 hours executing a randomly assigned human or LLM idea and wrote a 4-page paper, then reviewed blind.
numbers: Score change after execution (1-10): human about -0.01 novelty, +0.08 excitement, -0.05 effectiveness; AI -1.05 novelty, -1.76 excitement, -1.88 effectiveness. Post-execution excitement 3.90 AI vs 4.48 human; effectiveness 4.13 vs 4.78.
limits: AI drops larger on all four metrics (p<0.05). Ranking flip post execution not significant at N=43 ideas. Ideation-execution correlation weak; for AI excitement moderately negative. Small N, NLP only.
agent_relevance: Key warning: ideas that look novel before testing do not hold up after execution. Execute or simulate before trusting.

source: Lu et al. (2024) The AI Scientist: towards fully automated open-ended scientific discovery
finding: Pipeline: idea generation with novelty search, code edits via Aider, experiment runs, LaTeX paper writing, LLM review, archive loop. Applied to diffusion, language modeling, grokking.
numbers: Under $15 per paper. Diffusion table: Claude Sonnet 3.5 51 ideas, 49 novel, 38 papers, mean reviewer score 3.82, max 6.0, cost $250; GPT-4o 3.70; DeepSeek Coder 3.32 at $10; Llama-3.1 405B 2.30.
limits: Own limits: poor magnitude comparison, ignores metric changes vs baseline, hallucinated an ablation table and hardware details, weak citations. Authors advise not taking content at face value. Scores from its own LLM reviewer; human-made code templates.
agent_relevance: Whole-loop automation is feasible; its failure modes (hallucinated results, silent baseline mismatch) are guardrail targets.

source: Lu et al. (2024) AI Scientist automated reviewer validation
finding: GPT-4o reviewer with 5 self-reflection rounds and 5 ensembled reviews was tested on ICLR 2022 OpenReview papers.
numbers: At threshold 6: F1 0.57 vs 0.49 for humans, AUC 0.65 both. Balanced set: accuracy 0.65 vs 0.66, false negative rate 0.39 vs 0.52. Correlation of LLM score with average human score 0.18, between two humans 0.14. Cost $0.25 to $0.50 per review.
limits: Human accuracy in the NeurIPS 2021 consistency experiment was 73%, higher than the LLM on the imbalanced set. Weaker models (4o-mini, Llama 405B) did much worse. Human reviewer noise is high, so near-human is a low bar.
agent_relevance: An LLM critic approximates a noisy human critic; use as a filter, not truth.

source: Beel, Kan, Baumgart (2025) Evaluating Sakana's AI Scientist: bold claims, mixed results
finding: Independent test of the AI Scientist on a recommender-system task.
numbers: 5 of 12 proposed experiments (42%) failed from coding errors. Each iteration added only 8% more code characters. Median 5 citations per paper, only 5 of 34 citations from 2020 or later. Some ideas wrongly judged novel, such as micro-batching for SGD.
limits: An energy-efficiency experiment reported accuracy gains while using more compute, contradicting its goal. Missing figures, repeated sections, placeholder text. Small test, one domain, one student ran it.
agent_relevance: Independent replication shows keyword novelty search is weak and results can be logically flawed. Needs a claim-verification step.

source: Yamada et al. (2025) The AI Scientist-v2: workshop-level automated scientific discovery via agentic tree search
finding: Removes dependence on human code templates; uses agentic best-first tree search with a manager agent and a vision-language feedback loop on figures.
numbers: Three fully AI-written manuscripts were submitted to an ICLR workshop. One scored 6.33 on average (about top 45%) and would have been accepted; the other two scored lower and were not accepted.
limits: The accepted paper tested a compositional regularizer and found it did not reliably help. Workshop-level, not main track; n is 3.
agent_relevance: 1 in 3 pass rate at a low bar. Tree search over experiments helps but quality is limited.

source: Gottweis et al. (2025) Towards an AI co-scientist
finding: Gemini multi-agent system (generation, reflection, ranking tournament, evolution, proximity, meta-review) that scales test-time compute and ranks hypotheses by Elo.
numbers: Across 203 research goals, Elo of top hypotheses rose with time and showed no saturation. On 15 expert-curated hard goals it surpassed o1, o3-mini-high, DeepSeek R1, Gemini 2.0 and experts best guesses. For 11 expert-rated goals: preference rank 2.36, novelty 3.64, impact 3.09 out of 5.
limits: Elo is auto-evaluated by the system itself, not ground truth; authors say expert ratings are subjective. Circular selection.
agent_relevance: Generate-debate-rank-evolve loop is a template for our schema; an Elo tournament is a cheap relative critic.

source: Gottweis et al. (2025) Co-scientist wet-lab validations
finding: Experimental tests of proposed hypotheses.
numbers: AML repurposing: of five drugs tested in vitro, three (binimetinib, pacritinib, cerivastatin) reduced viability; binimetinib IC50 as low as 2 nM in AML lines, higher in non-AML TK6. KIRA6 IC50 10 nM in KG-1a vs 180 nM in TK6. For cf-PICI transfer it proposed interaction with diverse phage tails, reported as matching unpublished lab work.
limits: Only 3 of 5 drugs worked; the independent claim rests on the authors account; authors are the developers; cell-line tests are early stage.
agent_relevance: Hypothesis generation can yield testable leads; partial hit rate means each output needs a test plan.

source: Romera-Paredes et al. (2023) Mathematical discoveries from program search with LLMs (FunSearch)
finding: Evolutionary search over programs where an LLM proposes code and an automatic evaluator scores it; found new cap set lower bounds.
numbers: Not opened this session. Recalled only; exact numbers unverified.
limits: Needs a fast automatic scorer. Only problems with cheap verifiers.
agent_relevance: Pairing an LLM proposer with a hard verifier is a strong pattern; use for any checkable sub-claim.

source: Novikov et al. (2025) AlphaEvolve: a coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
finding: Evolutionary coding agent with a Gemini ensemble and automated evaluators; evolves whole programs.
numbers: Over 50 open math problems: matched best known in 75%, beat state of the art in 20%. 4x4 complex matrix multiply in 48 multiplications (improves Strassen 1969); kissing number in 11 dimensions raised to 593; improved 14 matrix multiplication settings. Production: 0.7% of Google fleet compute recovered, 23% kernel speedup, 1% cut in Gemini training time.
limits: Needs a machine-checkable evaluator; many matches are probably already optimal. Company self-report.
agent_relevance: Verifier-backed search yields real discoveries. Where no verifier exists, claims need extra guardrails.

source: Chen et al. (2025) ScienceAgentBench: rigorous assessment of language agents for data-driven scientific discovery
finding: 102 tasks from 44 peer-reviewed papers in 4 disciplines, checked by 9 experts; output is a Python program; 5 LLMs x 3 frameworks.
numbers: Best agent solved 32.4% independently and 34.3% with expert-provided knowledge (3 attempts). OpenAI o1-preview with more inference compute reached 42.2%.
limits: Direct prompting, OpenHands CodeAct and self-debug compared. Contamination mitigated by two strategies. Single-task code, not full discovery.
agent_relevance: Single steps of science are still hard. Claims of end-to-end automation are premature.

source: Majumder et al. (2024) DiscoveryBench: towards data-driven discovery with LLMs
finding: 264 real tasks from 6 domains plus 903 synthetic tasks; each is a dataset, metadata and a goal in natural language; scored on facets of the hypothesis.
numbers: Even the best agent scores only 25%.
limits: Domain knowledge matters (archaeology tasks). Economics (25%) and sociology (23%) higher; biology and engineering at 0%. Facet scoring uses LLM judging.
agent_relevance: Data-driven hypothesis search is hard without domain knowledge; our agent should retrieve domain priors.

source: Langley, Simon, Bradshaw, Zytkow (1987) Scientific Discovery: Computational Explorations of the Creative Process (BACON)
finding: BACON and successors rediscovered Kepler third law, Ohm law and others by heuristic search through data and term combinations.
numbers: Not opened; recalled. No numbers verified.
limits: Heuristics hand-coded; data cleaned and pre-selected by designers; critics say the designer supplied the representation.
agent_relevance: Origin of discovery as problem-space search; ties to Simon view in subfield 09.

source: Schmidt, Lipson (2009) Distilling free-form natural laws from experimental data (Eureqa)
finding: Genetic programming searches symbolic laws scored by fit and invariants; rediscovered laws of motion from pendulum data.
numbers: Not opened; recalled. Eureqa is the 71-of-100 baseline measured in AI Feynman (opened).
limits: Fit-only scoring can find fits with no meaning; parsimony needed.
agent_relevance: Fitness plus simplicity; evaluate on out-of-sample data.

source: King et al. (2009) The automation of science (Robot Scientist Adam)
finding: Closed-loop lab robot generated yeast gene function hypotheses and ran experiments.
numbers: Not opened; recalled. No numbers verified.
limits: Narrow domain, hand-built logical knowledge base.
agent_relevance: Hypothesis-experiment-update loop is the schema loop in embodied form.

source: Burger et al. (2020) A mobile robotic chemist
finding: Mobile robot ran Bayesian-optimised photocatalyst experiments over days.
numbers: Not opened; recalled. Numbers unverified.
limits: Search space bounded by humans.
agent_relevance: Bayesian optimisation over a bounded space is a baseline versus open-ended idea search.

source: Cross-source synthesis: where LLM discovery claims break
finding: Across Lu 2024, Si 2024/2025, Beel 2025, LLM-SRBench, ScienceAgentBench, DiscoveryBench: claims hold when a cheap evaluator exists, and fail when judged by execution or on unseen data.
numbers: Success: AlphaEvolve 20% new records; LLM-SR beats PySR with 2.5K vs 2M+ iterations. Failure: 31.5% best symbolic accuracy on unseen forms; 25% on DiscoveryBench; 32.4% on ScienceAgentBench; 42% experiment crash rate in an independent test.
limits: Synthesis of sources opened; not a new measurement. Different tasks, metrics and models.
agent_relevance: Design rule: pair every proposer with an external check; do not trust LLM self-judgement of novelty.

source: Cross-source: novelty judgment vs outcome
finding: Novelty rated before work does not predict outcome well.
numbers: Si 2024: AI novelty 5.64 vs human 4.84 pre-execution. Si 2025: AI novelty drop of 1.05 after execution, human about 0; correlation weak.
limits: Beel 2025: keyword novelty search marked known ideas as new. Different reviewer pools.
agent_relevance: Add an explicit prior-art check and an execution or simulation step before accepting a hypothesis.

source: Cross-source: memorisation in discovery benchmarks
finding: Textbook-equation tasks are poor tests for LLM discovery.
numbers: AI Feynman set (100 equations) is fully solved by symbolic regression and shows memorisation signs for LLMs; transformed set tops out at 31.5%.
limits: LLM-SR designed new tasks to prevent recitation. Memorisation evidence is from error curves.
agent_relevance: Test our agent on novel or transformed problems.

source: Cross-source: cost and compute scaling
finding: More test-time compute raises quality in several systems.
numbers: Co-scientist Elo no saturation; o1 raised ScienceAgentBench from 32.4% to 42.2%; AI Scientist paper under $15 but Sonnet diffusion run cost $250 for 51 ideas.
limits: Diversity saturates in simple over-generation (200 unique of 4000). Compute gains need a good selector.
agent_relevance: Spend extra compute on ranking and critique, not only more samples.
